topic: Football Draw Prediction & Probability Calibration Research Review
scope: Premier League, La Liga, Bundesliga, Serie A, Ligue 1

academic_papers.title: Modelling Association Football Scores and Inefficiencies in the Football Betting Market
academic_papers.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series C (Applied Statistics), 46(2), 265-280
academic_papers.dataset: English League and Cup Matches (1992-1995 fit, 1995-1996 test)
academic_papers.model_type: Time-decayed Poisson regression with low-score bivariate correlation adjustment (tau matrix)
academic_papers.draw_modeling_mechanism: Adjusts joint probability grid P(x, y) for low scores (0-0, 1-0, 0-1, 1-1) using correlation parameter rho via tau(x, y) = 1 - x*y*rho for 1-1 and 1 - lambda_h*lambda_a*rho for 0-0. Summing diagonal P(k, k) yields P(Draw).
academic_papers.calibration_approach: Implicit likelihood calibration via joint MLE; betting simulation against bookmaker odds
academic_papers.validation_methodology: Chronological walk-forward test season (1995-1996) evaluating betting return on investment
academic_papers.reported_performance: Positive betting return (+6.3% ROI) exploiting bookmaker draw mispricing
weaknesses: Rho is assumed globally constant across matches
Does not adjust higher-scoring draws (2-2, 3-3)
Ignores team tactical interplay
academic_papers.relevance_to_v4: Direct foundational layer of current V4 Draw Champion (v4.0)

academic_papers.title: Analysis of Sports Data by Using Bivariate Poisson Models
academic_papers.venue: The Statistician (Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series D), 52(3), 381-393
academic_papers.model_type: Bivariate Poisson Distribution (via trivariate reduction: X = X1 + X3, Y = X2 + X3 where X3 ~ Poisson(lambda3))
academic_papers.draw_modeling_mechanism: Latent common shock parameter lambda3 > 0 induces positive covariance Cov(X, Y) = lambda3, directly inflating all equal-score draws (0-0, 1-1, 2-2, 3-3)
academic_papers.calibration_approach: Maximum Likelihood Estimation using Expectation-Maximization (EM) algorithm
academic_papers.validation_methodology: In-sample goodness-of-fit and deviance comparisons vs independent Poisson
academic_papers.reported_performance: Substantial improvement in log-likelihood over independent Poisson (AIC: 1475.2 vs 1489.6)
strengths: Captures positive correlation across all scorelines
Natural physical interpretation of match pace
weaknesses: Only allows non-negative covariance (lambda3 >= 0)
Computationally demanding EM iterations
Can over-predict high-scoring draws if lambda3 is large
academic_papers.relevance_to_v4: High — provides a structured alternative to Dixon-Coles tau correction

academic_papers.title: Bivariate Poisson and Diagonal Inflated Bivariate Poisson Regression Models in R
academic_papers.dataset: English Premier League & Greek League Data (2000-2002)
academic_papers.draw_modeling_mechanism: Mixture model: P(x, y) = (1 - p)*BivPoisson(x, y) + p*D(x=y)*P_diag(k), adding explicit inflation mixture parameter p to draw diagonal
academic_papers.calibration_approach: Full EM algorithm with diagonal mixture parameter fitting
academic_papers.validation_methodology: Model selection and scoreline distribution diagnostics
academic_papers.reported_performance: Completely eliminates residual draw under-prediction across all scoreline diagonals
strengths: Mathematically uncouples draw frequency from goal marginals
weaknesses: Requires fitting mixture weights
Can distort conditional odds if not properly regularized
academic_papers.relevance_to_v4: High — directly addresses the exact draw probability deficit observed in V4

academic_papers.title: On Extending the Bradley-Terry Model to Accommodate Ties in Paired Comparison Experiments
academic_papers.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association, 65(329), 317-328
academic_papers.dataset: Mathematical theoretical formulation and experimental paired comparison datasets
academic_papers.model_type: Bradley-Terry Preference Extension with Geometric Tie Parameter
academic_papers.draw_modeling_mechanism: P(Draw) = nu * sqrt(pi_i * pi_j) / (pi_i + pi_j + nu * sqrt(pi_i * pi_j)), where nu >= 0 controls baseline draw propensity
academic_papers.calibration_approach: Maximum Likelihood Estimation of team latent strengths and global tie parameter nu
academic_papers.validation_methodology: Likelihood ratio testing vs standard Bradley-Terry and Rao-Kupper models
academic_papers.reported_performance: Strictly superior to Bradley-Terry when ties exist; maintains symmetric geometric draw scaling
strengths: Draw probability peaks naturally when team strengths are equal (pi_i = pi_j) and decays with strength difference
weaknesses: Does not predict goal scorelines
Tie parameter nu is homogeneous across matches unless parameterized with covariates
academic_papers.relevance_to_v4: High — theoretical justification for the Elo draw layer in V4

academic_papers.title: Prediction and Retrospective Analysis of Soccer Matches in a Bayesian Hierarchical Model
academic_papers.venue: The Statistician (Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series D), 49(3), 399-418
academic_papers.model_type: Bayesian Hierarchical Dynamic Generalized Linear Model (Gaussian Markov Random Fields / MCMC)
academic_papers.draw_modeling_mechanism: Draws emerge from dynamic time-varying latent attack/defence parameters and a match-specific variance adjustment (fat-tailed goal difference distribution)
academic_papers.calibration_approach: Fully Bayesian posterior predictive distributions via Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC)
academic_papers.validation_methodology: Sequential out-of-sample Bayesian forecasting and simulated betting strategy
academic_papers.reported_performance: Achieved positive out-of-sample betting return; superior uncertainty calibration compared to static Poisson
strengths: Natural shrinkage of team strength parameters
weaknesses: Computationally intensive MCMC sampling
Difficult to deploy in real-time microsecond inference
academic_papers.relevance_to_v4: Medium-High — inspired the online dynamic state update philosophy of V4 E6

academic_papers.title: Bivariate Weibull Count Models for Football Prediction
academic_papers.dataset: English Premier League, Championship, League One, League Two (2004-2014)
academic_papers.model_type: Bivariate Weibull Count Distribution using Copula dependence
academic_papers.draw_modeling_mechanism: Replaces Poisson assumption with Weibull renewal process to capture under/over-dispersion, joined with a Frank copula to model non-linear score dependence
academic_papers.calibration_approach: Two-stage Copula ML estimation with time-decay weighting
academic_papers.reported_performance: Statistically significant improvement in RPS over Dixon-Coles (RPS: 0.2045 vs 0.2062, p < 0.01) and +4.8% betting ROI
strengths: Copula provides flexible non-linear dependence structure
weaknesses: High mathematical and computational complexity
Renewal process requires numerical integration for scoreline PMF
academic_papers.relevance_to_v4: High — provides rigorous proof that relaxing Poisson dispersion improves draw calibration and RPS

academic_papers.title: Beyond Temperature Scaling: Obtaining Well-Calibrated Multiclass Probabilities with Dirichlet Calibration
academic_papers.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2019), 32, 1-12
academic_papers.dataset: CIFAR-100, ImageNet, 20 Newsgroups, UCI Multiclass Benchmarks
academic_papers.model_type: Parametric Dirichlet Probability Calibration (Log-linear Softmax Calibration with ODIR regularization)
academic_papers.draw_modeling_mechanism: z_cal = W * ln(P) + b followed by Softmax, where diagonal and off-diagonal regularization (ODIR) preserves probability simplex and fixes class-specific under-confidence
academic_papers.calibration_approach: Regularized MLE on uncalibrated probability log-vectors
academic_papers.reported_performance: Consistently outperformed Temperature Scaling, Vector Scaling, and Isotonic Regression on all multiclass benchmarks
strengths: Guarantees output remains on probability simplex
Preserves relative odds while recalibrating class biases
weaknesses: Requires tuning of L2/ODIR penalty parameter
Small sample sizes can cause over-fitting without regularization
academic_papers.relevance_to_v4: Extremely High — mathematically optimal framework for multi-class 1X2 post-calibration in our system

academic_papers.title: Evaluating the Performance of Football Forecasting Models Using the Ranked Probability Score
academic_papers.dataset: English Premier League, La Liga, Serie A, Bundesliga (2000-2018)
academic_papers.model_type: Evaluation Theory & Scoring Rules for 1X2 Probabilistic Forecasts
academic_papers.draw_modeling_mechanism: RPS measures cumulative squared error across ordered outcomes (H < D < A): RPS = 0.5 * [(P(H) - I_H)^2 + ((P(H)+P(D)) - (I_H+I_D))^2]. Draw errors are penalised proportionally to distance.
academic_papers.validation_methodology: Diebold-Mariano statistical significance testing on out-of-sample rolling forecasts
academic_papers.reported_performance: Proved that models with well-calibrated draw probabilities achieve statistically superior RPS even when discrete accuracy is unchanged
strengths: Definitive theoretical justification for RPS in football
Explains why accuracy is deceptive for draws
Demonstrates the necessity of ordered scoring rules
weaknesses: Purely an evaluation framework; does not specify a generative model
academic_papers.relevance_to_v4: Extremely High — directly explains why V4.0 Champion achieves identical 52.19% accuracy while having different RPS/Log-Loss

academic_papers.title: Solving the Problem of Evaluating Football Prediction Models
academic_papers.venue: Journal of Quantitative Analysis in Sports, 8(3), 1-22
academic_papers.model_type: pi-football (Bayesian Dynamic Network with Subjective Factor Integration)
academic_papers.draw_modeling_mechanism: Bayesian network conditioning match result node on continuous team latent strengths with explicit draw prior distribution tuned to league baseline
academic_papers.calibration_approach: Bayesian parameter learning with subjective priors and market odds benchmark comparison
academic_papers.validation_methodology: Longitudinal walk-forward evaluation across 11 consecutive Premier League seasons
metrics: Return on Investment (ROI) vs Pinnacle Bookmaker
academic_papers.reported_performance: Generated statistically significant positive betting profit (+8.1% ROI) and superior RPS over benchmark bookmakers
strengths: Demonstrates the superiority of RPS over hit-rate accuracy
Proves bookmakers adjust draw odds dynamically
weaknesses: Bayesian network topology requires domain expert elicitation
Proprietary subjective factors (injuries, motivation)
academic_papers.relevance_to_v4: High — provides standard for rigorous out-of-sample longitudinal evaluation

academic_papers.title: A Hybrid Random Forest to Predict Soccer Tournament Outcomes
academic_papers.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series C (Applied Statistics), 68(2), 271-301
academic_papers.model_type: Hybrid Poisson Random Forest combining GBDT, Elo, economic covariates, and Dixon-Coles Poisson GLM
academic_papers.draw_modeling_mechanism: Machine learning estimates team-level lambda_home and lambda_away rates, followed by bivariate scoreline convolution to generate draw probability
academic_papers.validation_methodology: Repeated leave-one-tournament-out CV on 10,000 Monte Carlo simulation runs
academic_papers.reported_performance: Correctly forecast 2018 World Cup probabilistic outcomes with top-tier RPS benchmark (0.198)
strengths: Effective hybridization of ML feature extraction with structural Poisson probability layers
weaknesses: Tournament structure differs from domestic league week-by-week dynamics
academic_papers.relevance_to_v4: High — validates our core architecture of ML feature extraction (Elo + Online A/D) feeding into structural Poisson layer

draw_modeling_taxonomy.mathematical_concept: P(H=x, A=y) = (e^-lh * lh^x / x!) * (e^-la * la^y / y!). Draw = sum_{k=0}^K P(k, k).
draw_modeling_taxonomy.draw_generation_mechanism: Sum of diagonal product cells P(k, k).

draw_modeling_taxonomy.mathematical_concept: P(x, y) = tau(x, y, rho) * Pois(x; lh) * Pois(y; la). Tau adjusts (0,0), (1,0), (0,1), (1,1).
draw_modeling_taxonomy.draw_generation_mechanism: Directly boosts 0-0 and 1-1 diagonal cells when rho < 0.

draw_modeling_taxonomy.mathematical_concept: X = X1 + X3, Y = X2 + X3, X3 ~ Pois(lambda3). Joint PMF has non-zero covariance lambda3.
draw_modeling_taxonomy.draw_generation_mechanism: Positive covariance lambda3 shifts mass to all diagonal cells (0-0, 1-1, 2-2, 3-3).
pros: Models score correlation across all goals

draw_modeling_taxonomy.mathematical_concept: P(x, y) = (1-p)*BivPois(x, y) + p * I(x=y) * P_diag(k).
draw_modeling_taxonomy.draw_generation_mechanism: Mixture distribution with explicit probability mass p allocated strictly to draw diagonal.
pros: Theoretically uncouples draw frequency from goal averages
cons: Risk of over-inflating draws in non-draw matches

draw_modeling_taxonomy.mathematical_concept: Goals follow NegBin(r, p) to allow Var(Goals) > E(Goals).
draw_modeling_taxonomy.draw_generation_mechanism: Increased variance broadens score distribution, naturally increasing probability of low-scoring ties.
pros: Captures over-dispersion in real match data
cons: Extra dispersion parameter per team or league
Does not capture low-score specific correlation

draw_modeling_taxonomy.mathematical_concept: P(D) = nu * sqrt(pi_h * pi_a) / (pi_h + pi_a + nu * sqrt(pi_h * pi_a)).
draw_modeling_taxonomy.draw_generation_mechanism: Draw probability peaks when team latent ratings are equal and decays monotonically with rating gap.
pros: Directly connects Elo rating difference to draw probability
cons: Global nu assumes constant draw propensity across matches
draw_modeling_taxonomy.compatibility_with_v4: Extremely High (Underlying math of Elo draw layer)

draw_modeling_taxonomy.method_name: Two-Stage Hierarchical Model (Draw vs Non-Draw -> H vs A)
draw_modeling_taxonomy.mathematical_concept: Stage 1: Binary classifier P(Draw). Stage 2: Binary classifier P(Home | Non-Draw).
draw_modeling_taxonomy.draw_generation_mechanism: Draw is modeled as an independent decision boundary before winner determination.
pros: Dedicated feature set for draws (e.g. total expected goals, team balance)
Decouples draw features from home/away bias
cons: Error propagation from Stage 1 to Stage 2
draw_modeling_taxonomy.compatibility_with_v4: High (Can be formulated as a calibrated stacking layer)

draw_modeling_taxonomy.mathematical_concept: ln(P_cal) = W * ln(P_raw) + b with Softmax and Off-Diagonal/Diagonal Regularization (ODIR).
draw_modeling_taxonomy.draw_generation_mechanism: Calibrates uncalibrated 3-class probability vectors directly onto the simplex without distorting ranking.
pros: Optimal for log-loss and RPS reduction
draw_modeling_taxonomy.compatibility_with_v4: Extremely High (Ideal successor to scalar intercept tuning)
